in Babylon, which is Fustat,
"I am not clad in a tunic like Cyrus, that I should give you gold,
but only weapons."
And when the envoys returned empty-handed to Umar,
Manuel took fright, abandoned Egypt, and fled,
and the Arabs gained control over Egypt.
And in the fifteenth year of the Arabs (636 of our Lord?), Umar came to Palestine,
and Sophronius, Bishop of Jerusalem, came out to meet him.
And he received terms of assurance for the whole region,
and he even wrote a document (sigillion) for him,
and that no Jew had authority to dwell in Jerusalem.
And when Umar entered Jerusalem,
he commanded, and a mosque for their prayer was built on the site of Solomon's Temple.
And when the Bishop saw that Umar was dressed in dirty garments,
he urged him earnestly to accept from him a garment and a linen robe,
and brought them before him,
but he was not willing.
This man was completely just and far from greed,
and although they had gained power over all the treasures of the Persians and Romans,
he did not change his former austerity.
And from there he passed through the cities of Syria and subdued all of them,
and crossed the Euphrates to the East.
And the people of Edessa came out,
and secured terms of assurance {OCR?: ܘܫܩܠܘ} for their city.
However, Thella (Tella) and Dara, which did not submit {OCR?: ܐܫܠܡ},
he took by battle,
and killed the Romans who were in them.
And in the nineteenth year of the Arabs,
Umar ordered that all the lands of his domain be inscribed for the poll-tax.
And in that same year, which was the year 951
of the Greeks [AD 640],
Heraclius died.
And Constantine (the Third?), his elder son, reigned four months.
And Martina, his father's wife, killed him with poison,
and made her young son Heraclonas king,
who was called, they say, the New David.
And it seemed evil to the Senate,
and they deposed Heraclonas,
and made Constas {OCR?: ܩܘܣܛܢܣ}, the son of the murdered man, king.
This man killed both his uncles and Martina, the wife of Heraclius.
Now Umar reigned twelve years.
A certain servant, a polisher (or stonemason),
having complained to him several times against his master,
and he neglected him,
struck him with a knife in his belly while he was praying,
and he died.
[Uthman reigned] twelve years.
This man began to act greedily and to amass gold for himself,
and the Arabs planned to kill him.
